original.reason: The ray intersection of an arbitrary convex hull need not be of the form [0,R]: it can be empty or [a,R] with a>0, so the asserted equivalences with t≤R are false. Also, one orthogonal map cannot generally send two arbitrary non-collinear points p,q simultaneously to re,se. The theorem itself remains valid.

judgment.reason: Its essential radial-depth lemma is not established. The proposed Steiner-symmetrization argument does not define the relevant joint sample-space symmetrization or justify the claimed comparison of membership events/measures; iterating over a basis does not fill these gaps.

The asserted symmetrization fact is the substantive theorem and is only sketched. Conditioning and noting that sections of convex sets are intervals does not justify that the convex-hull membership event has the required convex interval sections in sample-coordinate space, nor the claimed comparison after centering.

The convex-hull depth lemma is invoked without a complete proof. The brief interval-symmetrization description does not specify or justify a measure-preserving transformation of the joint sample space and does not establish the required event inclusion/comparison.

The central radial monotonicity theorem is not rigorously proved. In particular, the claim that convex-hull membership is convex in each sample coordinate is unsupported and generally problematic, and the stated Steiner-symmetrization argument does not derive the displayed inequality.
